name: isputnik
description: Private self-hosted family media library, now in Beta (4.0.0 and later). Audiobooks with a built-in player, ebooks with an in-browser reader, and a photo and video gallery with on-device face recognition, albums, slideshows rendered to MP4, and a Photo Inbox for scans and photos from relatives. The family writes its own stories and recipes around what the house holds, and keeps a family tree linked to the people found in the photos. Multiple accounts with per-person progress and permissions, sharing and guest links, passkeys and two-factor sign-in, an installable PWA with offline listening, and an English or Russian interface. Beta means your data is looked after: the database migrates itself forward on every upgrade, a copy of it is saved before each new version starts, and backups can be scheduled from the Control panel. Features are still moving. On first run, open the web UI on your home network to create the administrator account.

paths.name: Config & Data
paths.description: Stores database, metadata, thumbnails, backups, settings, and application data. Backups appear here under backups/.

paths.name: Media Storage
paths.description: Media storage path. Must be Read/Write — uploading photos/videos and filing them into dated folders writes here (scanning alone only needs read). Additional storage locations can be added later by editing the container or from within iSputnik.

ports.name: Web UI Port
ports.description: Port used to access the iSputnik web interface.

variables.name: PUID
variables.description: User ID the app runs as. The server runs unprivileged (not root); on first start it takes ownership of the Config & Data path as this user. 99 (nobody) matches the default owner of an Unraid appdata share — leave it unless your share is owned by a different user.

variables.name: PGID
variables.description: Group ID the app runs as. 100 (users) matches the default group of an Unraid appdata share — leave it unless your share uses a different group.

variables.name: App URL
variables.description: The address the app is reached at (for example https://isputnik.example.com). Set this when you put a reverse proxy or tunnel in front: it fixes the browser origin the app accepts, and an https address is also what turns on HTTPS-only enforcement (HSTS). Leave blank for plain LAN access.

variables.name: HSTS
variables.description: Leave blank. When App URL starts with https:// the app tells browsers to stay on HTTPS for a year. Set to false to suppress that — for example when your reverse proxy already sends its own Strict-Transport-Security header. Nothing is sent for a plain-http App URL either way.

variables.name: Cookie Secure
variables.description: Leave on auto: secure cookies then follow App URL — on when it starts with https://, off for a plain http home install. Set true or false only to override that. Secure cookies are never sent over plain http, so forcing true on an http install drops the sign-in cookie and you cannot log in. (auto needs version 1.13.3 or newer.)

variables.name: Session Length (days)
variables.description: Number of days a login session remains valid.

variables.name: Linked Device Session Length (days)
variables.description: Number of days a TV, wall display or other screen signed in with Link a device stays signed in. Each one is listed under Profile, Devices and can be revoked there.

variables.name: Invite Validity (days)
variables.description: Number of days invitation links remain valid.

variables.name: Trusted Proxy Addresses
variables.description: The reverse proxy's own IP or CIDR range, comma-separated for several (e.g. 172.18.0.0/16 for a Docker network). Preferred over Trusted Proxy Hops: forwarded headers are only believed when they come from these addresses. Leave blank for direct LAN access. Needed for correct per-IP rate limiting, auto-block, and trusted networks.

variables.name: Trusted Proxy Hops
variables.description: Alternative to Trusted Proxy Addresses when the proxy's IP isn't fixed: the number of reverse proxies in front of the app (usually 1 behind a reverse proxy or Cloudflare Tunnel). Leave blank for direct LAN access or when Trusted Proxy Addresses is set (addresses win if both are). Set it to match your proxy count, no higher, and don't expose the app's port directly.

variables.name: Games URL
variables.description: Where the optional isputnik.games container answers, as seen from this container (e.g. http://isputnik-games:4200 on a shared Docker network). Leave blank for no games. Both this and the Games Gateway Secret must be set for the Games entry to appear.

variables.name: Games Gateway Secret
variables.description: A long random string shared with the games container (its GATEWAY_SECRET). Every request this app forwards to the games carries it, so the games server knows who is signed in came from here.
